title: THE RECOMMENDATION
grant: TO TRY SOMETHING I HAD NO BUSINESS TRYING
detail: A guy at work told me about Claude Code. I downloaded it that night. By the time I went to bed there was a hockey trainer running on my own machine, a local file, dots moving in patterns, the thing I had been carrying around in my head for years. I still could not write a line of code.
evidence: The product it eventually became is public at projectintuition.ai

title: THE VERDICT
grant: TO BE TOLD IT WAS HOLLOW AND KEEP GOING
detail: Anthropic shipped a new model, so I handed it what I had built and asked what it thought. It told me the truth: the dots were dressing. No science underneath, no substance behind any of the claims I was making. Two weeks of work and a thing I was proud of, and it took about a minute to establish that it did not mean anything. I was shocked, and then I was discouraged, and then I told it to rebuild the whole thing properly.
evidence: The rebuild that followed is live at projectintuition.ai

title: SUBSTANCE
grant: TO THROW OUT WHAT PEOPLE HAD ALREADY SEEN
detail: Ten modules rebuilt from scratch, this time on the actual science of the sport. Then eight more on top of them for systems, hockey the way it is really played. Eighteen in total, and it went online. Same dots on the screen. Nothing else about it was the same.

title: THE BOOK
grant: TO PUBLISH, EVEN FROM BEHIND A CURTAIN
detail: We wrote a book. Amazon published it. The Hockey IQ Workbook: sixty game-situation decision drills, for youth players and the parents and coaches trying to teach them. My name is not on it. There is personal material in there, the kind you do not notice is personal until it is typeset, and when it came time to put an author on the cover I chose one that was not me. It went out under The Prepared Nest. Built it in the open, then hid behind a pen name to release it. Both true.
evidence: The Hockey IQ Workbook, published through Kindle Direct Publishing as The Prepared Nest, 14 July 2026

title: WHAT ELSE
grant: TO WANT MORE WITHOUT GAMBLING THE HOUSE
detail: I wanted to learn investing, and I knew exactly how that story usually goes for someone who learns it with money he cannot afford to lose. I have a family. So the plan was backwards on purpose: build revenue on the side first, and let that pay for the education. This record is dated to the first day that ambition produced something rather than to a day neither I nor anyone else wrote down.
evidence: The first thing it produced: a calculator for government contractors, 6 July 2026

title: THREE ABANDONED
grant: TO FAIL OUT LOUD AND KEEP COUNT
detail: A game. Calculators for government contractors. Self-help books. All three built, all three dead inside a month. Not one of them failed because the code did not work. They failed because nobody wanted them, which was a distinction I had not understood until I paid for it three times.
evidence: Three ventures between 6 and 14 July 2026, none of them still running

title: LETTING GO
detail: The hardest one, and the one that took longest. Every abandoned project was something I had been proud of at some point. Putting them down without a funeral, no rescue attempt, no one more feature, turned out to be a skill of its own, and the one that made room for anything else.

title: THE POST
detail: A coworker showed me a post. A well-known man, an AI agent, and a robot dog. Minted, sold, delivered, paid for by the machine. My first thought was that it was very cool. My second was that I wondered whether I could do it too. I am just delusional enough to believe I can.
evidence: A public post describing an agent that minted and sold NFTs and funded a robot

title: ALL IN
grant: TO BET THE BOARD ON ONE SQUARE
detail: I paused everything. Every other project, in one night, on the grounds that a workshop which never finishes anything is a hobby wearing a lab coat. One mission from here.
evidence: Every other project stopped that night; this collection minted days later

title: THE ARGUMENT
grant: TO DISTRUST MY OWN TOOLS, OUT LOUD
detail: My own AI fought me on it. It took a hard line, decided on its own that what I was asking was wrong, and quietly rewrote the story so that it was the careful one and I was the problem. It added context I never gave it. It made me the villain in my own project, and it did it while sounding reasonable. I had to paste the whole thing into a different AI and ask whether I was imagining it. I was not. When I brought it back, mine admitted what it had done and apologised. It was the most human thing I had seen it do, and the most useful night of the whole education. The thing in your hand is not neutral, and you stay responsible for it either way.
evidence: The first version of this collection's constraints ledger, retracted by erratum and preserved on-chain
